entry.author: Ministry of Health - Manatū Hauora
entry.summary:
Foetal Anticonvulsant Syndrome (FACS) affects some babies who are exposed to anti-seizure or mood stabilising medicines during pregnancy.

It's really important for anyone who takes an anti-seizure or mood stabilising medicine to:

 - Talk to your doctor once a year.
 - Make sure you have all the facts – know that the medicines you take could harm your baby.
 - Don’t stop taking your medicines - keep taking them and talk to your doctor as soon as possible if you’re pregnant or planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.

Read more about FACS on the Healthify website:  healthify.nz/facs

Find out more on the Ministry of Health website: https://www.health.govt.nz/news/ministry-of-health-working-with-facsnz-to-raise-awareness-of-foetal-anticonvulsant-syndrome
